scenes.heading: Debugging Distributed Failures
scenes.subheading: Finding the needle in Spark & streaming
scenes.narration: Debugging distributed pipelines means finding a single failing task among thousands, where the symptom is often far from the true cause.

scenes.heading: Classic distributed failure modes
bullets: Data skew: one partition dwarfs the rest
Stragglers: a few slow tasks hold up the stage
OOM: executors killed under memory pressure
Shuffle spill: too much data crossing the network
scenes.narration: Data skew is the classic killer, where one partition holds most of the data and one task runs forever. Stragglers are a few slow tasks that hold up an entire stage. Out-of-memory errors kill executors under pressure, excessive shuffle spills flood the network, and in streaming, backpressure builds when consumers fall behind the incoming rate.

scenes.heading: A debugging workflow
scenes.narration: Start by reading the actual error and identifying which stage failed rather than guessing. Open the Spark UI to see task-level timing and shuffle sizes. Look for the skewed partition or straggler task, inspect the physical plan to understand the shuffle, and then fix it by repartitioning, salting the skewed key, or tuning memory.

scenes.heading: Symptom vs root cause
scenes.narration: The symptom you see is usually a slow job, a stalled stage, or an executor that keeps dying. The root cause is almost always upstream of that symptom, like a skewed join key, a bad partition count, or executors that are simply too small. Good debugging is the discipline of tracing the visible symptom back to that real cause.

scenes.text: In distributed systems the slowest task defines the runtime. Hunt for skew and stragglers before you throw more hardware at it.
scenes.narration: In distributed systems the single slowest task defines the whole runtime, so hunt for skew and stragglers before you reflexively throw more hardware at the problem.
